newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 27.

text.p: PRAVO - Parliament approved a law for public health insurance, which will be in effect from April. The new law means that patients will continue to make payment in cash for medicines, that patients can see a specialist without recommendation from a general physician and without paying extra charges, and that the amount which invalids are reimbursed for health aid will increase.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Komercni Banka (KB) is interested in increasing the share of foreign investors in the company to 12 percent through global deposit certificates. The Bank of New York, which is the depositary of KB shares, requested that the Czech National Bank increase the limit for issuing certificates.

- Companies which mine brown coal recorded stability in their operations for the first time since 1990 last year. Last year, 58.77 million tons of brown coal were mined in the Czech Republic, and for the first time in many years, the industry did not have a year-on-year decline.

- The mining companies Severoceske Doly, Sokolovska Uhelna and Mostecka Uhelna will present penalty invoices to Czech Railways for losses amounting to 167 million crowns caused by the railway strike in February.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Parliament approved a new law which will change the Czech-Slovak border. The area U Sabotu will now become part of Slovakia, and the Czech Republic will finally have a defined Eastern border.

- Friday, February 28, is the last day for owners of motor vehicles to pay for liability insurance at the normal rate. Most rates for liability insurance from Ceska Pojistovna, which has a monopoly on this kind of insurance, will increase on average by 22 percent and in some cases by 51 percent.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The cabinet coalition will address deregulation of energy prices and rents. Those who know the new prices, which will be announced to the public at the conference, said that the differing opinions of individual parties will not affect under what conditions their voters will have to live.

- Chances for many businesses to obtain bank credits decreased at the end of last year. While during the first half of 1996, the amount of money issued to businesses in credit increased by 48.6 billion crowns, between July and November it increased by only 3.3 billion.
